[USER] User is looking for tips on how to improve finger independence on the piano.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Finger independence is a crucial aspect of piano playing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Developing finger independence takes time, patience, and consistent practice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended exercises for finger independence include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Finger Isolation Exercises: Lift each finger one at a time, keeping the others still.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Hanon Exercises: A set of 60 exercises designed to improve finger strength, dexterity, and independence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Finger Alternation Exercises: Play a C major scale with alternating fingers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Chromatic Scales: Play a chromatic scale with each hand separately.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Broken Chord Exercises: Play a C major chord broken into individual notes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Finger Substitution Exercises: Play a simple melody using different fingers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Slow Practice: Practice exercises at a slow tempo for precision.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Mirror Practice: Use a mirror to observe hand position and finger movement.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Relaxation and Flexibility: Keep hands and arms relaxed and practice stretches.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Practice Regularly: Set aside time each day for exercises (10-15 minutes).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended classical piano pieces for beginners include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Chopin's Preludes (Op. 28, Nos. 1-3)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Bach's Inventions (BWV 772-786)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Mozart's Sonatinas (K. 281, 282, 283)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Beethoven's Sonatina in G major (Op. 49, No. 1)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Clementi's Sonatinas (Op. 36, Nos. 1-3)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Schubert's Impromptus (Op. 142, Nos. 1-3)
